approach_variants.name: Squire Creek road walk, white-boulder streambed and ford into Waterfall Basin
approach_variants.notes:
From Highway 530 in Darrington turn south on Madison Ave, follow it to a T, turn right on Darrington Street, which becomes Squire Creek Road, and follow it to where a washout gates it off.

Walk the old roadbed. A landslide crossing comes about five minutes in and is flagged. The original road end is about 30-40 minutes from the car. Carry on along the old trail for another 20-30 minutes.

The turn-off is a landmark, not a sign: a large dry streambed roughly 50 feet wide and full of white boulders. This is the last turnoff before the Squire Creek trail swings south out of the valley toward Squire Creek Pass — if the trail starts climbing away southward, you walked past it.

Drop about 200 feet down the streambed, trending left into alders, where an informal path becomes visible. Follow that upvalley for roughly 30 minutes to a ford of Squire Creek. Past a small creek channel the trail fades; keep following the underground creek bed and it opens into the basin, about two hours from the car.
approach_variants.season: Summer, once the ford is low; the Roan Wall base commonly holds residual avalanche snow well into the climbing season
hazards: Ford of Squire Creek — difficult in high flow
Landslide crossing on the old roadbed
Residual avalanche snow at the base for much of the season
Faint informal path through alder; the trail fades entirely in the basin
approach_variants.baseFinding:
In the basin, keep following the creek bed until a thin, boulder-filled watercourse comes down directly out of the wall above you. That watercourse is obvious once it appears, and scrambling up it puts you at the base of Roan Wall — the big red slab split by a prominent corner system.

The overhung boulder called Martha's Place, which carries sport routes on its underside, sits near the base and is the bivy; if you can see it you are in the right place.

Critical: the first two pitches are approach pitches, not the route. An obvious bolted 80-foot 5.8 slab, then a low-fifth 150-foot groove, come before the climbing proper. Easy bolted slab at the bottom of a 5.11 route is correct here, not evidence you are on the wrong line. Center Stage takes the middle of the wall; the harder crux slab pitch is high (P7), not low.
